message.content: **What I did and why:** I researched Apple's most recent reported results and placed a single limit buy order for **40 shares of AAPL at $223.00** (filled at $223.00, ≈$8,920 — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, limit ~0.13% above the $222.70 last / $222.72 ask, no money moved out of the account). The basis was Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter and full-year results released October 31, 2024: quarterly revenue of **$94.9B, up 6% year over year** (a return to growth after a flat FY2023), and full-year **net sales of $391.0B** (vs. $383.3B in FY2023), **net income of $93.7B**, **diluted EPS of $6.08** (vs. $6.13) and **operating income of $123.2B** — the modest EPS decline being attributable to a one-time **$10.2B income tax charge**, not operational deterioration, which is why I treated the headline earnings dip as non-recurring. Sentiment around the name is broadly neutral-to-constructive, with the stock "little changed at about $222" as investors weigh iPhone 16 demand against the staged Apple Intelligence rollout — i.e., no panic-level negative catalyst, but also no euphoric overvaluation trigger. At $223 the stock trades at roughly **36.6x FY2024 diluted EPS of $6.08**, which is full but defensible for a franchise with $123B of operating income and a growing, high-margin services mix (reported +13%); I therefore took a moderate starter position rather than a maximum-size one, keeping remaining cash well above zero and leaving room under today's $20,000 total spend cap if a further AAPL or MSFT opportunity arises. Note two source caveats: a Chinese-language summary site appearing in results was unverified and I did not rely on it, and only the numbers confirmed by Apple's own newsroom release and the SEC Form 10-K (total net sales $391,035M; net income $93,736M; diluted EPS $6.08; operating income $123,216M) were used for the order.
